page: Google Cloud Platform c2-standard-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, this instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The processor features a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 24 MB L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AES cryptography. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities alongside constrained multi-core scaling. The instance achieves average tier results in single-core stress-ng (1572.39) and Geekbench single-core (1309.0) tests. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2855.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 18.77 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with large-block read and write speeds measuring 28.26 GB/sec and 24.11 GB/sec respectively.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and moderate single-threaded performance, the c2-standard-4 is suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive parallelization or high memory bandwidth. Appropriate use cases include single-threaded text processing, light software compilation, and small-scale web serving. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated CPU cores provide predictable execution times for compute-focused tasks, though the lack of local storage and modest multi-core scaling represent clear tradeoffs for database or highly parallelized operations.
